issues.description: The problem statement (and UML) requires the Animal constructor and the name getter/setter to have protected visibility, but the solution implements a public constructor and public getName()/setName() methods. This visibility mismatch can confuse students about the intended encapsulation and inheritance design and may lead them to implement incorrect access modifiers.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the implementation and the specification consistent. Either update the problem statement/UML to require a public Animal constructor and public getName()/setName(), or change the solution (and template) so Animal's constructor and the name getter/setter use protected visibility. Preferably, align the solution with the UML requirement by making the constructor and the getter/setter protected to match the stated encapsulation intent.
